# 13 — Collection metadata and `contractURI`

<!-- generated:status-banner -->

> **RC6 is PREPARED_NOT_DEPLOYED.** RC6 is not deployed on any chain. Every RC6 contract address is still to be determined and will change; this repository publishes none.
> Public creator launch is **closed** on all 4 configured chains.

Two different things are called "metadata" in a launch, and conflating them is how a creator ends up
with a collection that renders on chain and shows a blank tile on every marketplace.

| Surface | What it is | Where it is computed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tokenURI(id)` | The artwork. Base64 JSON with an embedded base64 SVG. | On chain, at read time, from the immutable art binding and live hook state |
| `contractURI()` | Collection-level profile media — name, description, cover, banner, links. Marketplace furniture. | A content-addressed document, resolved and re-verified on every read |

This page is about the second one.

## The two digests, and only one of them reaches a chain

<!-- generated:metadata-commitment -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

| Value | Where it lives | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metadataUriHash` | `LaunchParams`, on chain | keccak256(bytes(uri)) - the hash of the URI STRING, and nothing else. |
| `metadataContentHash` | the `.relics` bundle and the studio, off chain | A content digest over the metadata JSON, carried by the .relics bundle. It NEVER reaches a chain. |

Two digests exist and they are not interchangeable. An earlier draft named the on-chain field metadataContentHash, which put a name meaning one quantity on a field holding the other. If you see that name in a chain context, it is the wrong one.

- Zero `metadataUriHash` is **refused** at the launch gate.
- `contractURI()` is non-empty in the launch receipt state: **yes**.
- A second, post-launch metadata-bind transaction: **no**. RC5 had a post-launch bindMetadataRegistry step. RC6 does not carry that path at all: LaunchPolicyV1 refuses a launch whose metadataUriHash is zero, and the collection's bindBirthMetadata runs inside the same CREATE2 call that creates the proxy.
- metadataUriHash is not a CREATE2 salt and not part of any component's initializer calldata, so changing a project's metadata leaves its token, collection and mined hook addresses exactly where they were.

<!-- /generated:metadata-commitment -->

If you are holding a value called `metadataContentHash` and about to put it in calldata, stop: that
is the wrong one. An earlier draft of the interface used that name for the on-chain field, which put
a name meaning one quantity on a field holding the other — and the repair somebody reaches for when
a "hash mismatch" is not a mismatch at all is to loosen the check until it passes.

## The sequence

Every step below is implemented server-side and happens **before** the creator signs anything.

1. **The creator supplies or generates the media.** The studio offers two sources: generate a cover
   deterministically from the artwork itself, or upload an image file. There is no
   "paste an image URL" path — the media slots structurally cannot hold an `https://` URL, and a
   launch gate refuses any scheme that is not a content address.
2. **The exact media bytes are pinned**, and a claimed pin is re-verified rather than believed: the
   server re-retrieves each claimed content address and re-hashes what comes back, demoting the
   claim on any failure.
3. **The metadata document is rebuilt canonically on the server**, from the validated fields — not
   accepted from the client. A document that would fail the launch gate is never pinned, because
   pinning is permanent.
4. **The document is pinned, then read back independently** by the content address the pin provider
   returned, over the read path rather than the write path, and the returned bytes are compared
   against the declared digest and re-parsed as JSON. A mismatch is a distinct, named failure; so is
   "pinned, but the read-back failed", which is not the same state as "never pinned".
5. **The resolver key is derived from the canonical URI** — `keccak256(bytes(uri))` — and computed
   exactly once, on the server. The front end never computes it.
6. **One launch transaction.** `metadataUriHash` travels inside `LaunchParams`. The launch policy
   refuses a zero value, and the collection's `bindBirthMetadata` runs **inside the same CREATE2
   call that creates the collection proxy**, so a launch whose metadata cannot be resolved dies
   wholesale — taking the token, the hook, the pool and the registry record with it.

The property that sequence buys is worth stating exactly: **there is no state in which an RC6
project exists and its collection answers `contractURI()` with the empty string.** That is why there
is no second creator transaction in which somebody has to remember to fix it.

### The resolver is not trusted, and nothing here asks it to be

`bindBirthMetadata` will only store bytes whose `keccak256` equals the committed hash. A substituted
resolver — hostile, wrong, or simply not the pinned one — can make the launch **revert**, and can
never make the collection serve a document the creator did not sign. Producing different bytes at
the same digest is a keccak256 preimage collision, not a transaction.

`contractURI()` re-proves this on **every read**, not once at birth: whatever the resolver returns,
the only bytes that leave the function are bytes whose hash is the committed digest. Bytes that are
not are indistinguishable from no metadata, and are reported as none.

And the writer cannot choose the key. The resolver derives `key = keccak256(bytes(uri))` itself from
the bytes being published, so there is no key-squatting position to take.

## What RC5 did, and why RC6 does not carry it

RC5 had a second path: `bindMetadataRegistry`, a post-launch one-shot the rights owner called to
point a collection at a registry. It is gone, and not because the fix was insufficient.

A registry bind is only meaningful on a collection that launched **without** metadata, and no RC6
collection can. So the path would have been unreachable runtime guarding a storage slot that is
always zero — two surfaces answering `contractURI()`, maintained separately, agreeing until the day
they did not.

If you are reading an integration written against RC5, two consequences follow. There is no
post-launch metadata-bind step to schedule. And an RC5-era verifier that expects
`contractURI()` to return a `data:application/json;utf8,…` payload will fail a perfectly healthy RC6
collection, which returns a content-addressed URI string.

## Changing your metadata does not move your addresses

`metadataUriHash` is not a CREATE2 salt, not an init-code argument, and not part of any component's
initializer calldata. Changing a project's metadata leaves its token, collection and mined hook
addresses exactly where they were.

That is a requirement rather than an accident. Other launchpads have put the image URL into
constructor arguments and made the token address a function of it; a creator who then fixed a typo
in their cover got a different token.

## Who controls the collection afterwards

`owner()` on the collection is ERC-173 **attribution and permitted metadata control only**. It reads
the `ProjectRights` token directly, so it moves with a sale of the project, every time, with no
contract sitting in between. It is explicitly **not** an upgrade authority — that is the Safe's, and
this function never returns it — and it is not a privileged role over `awaken`, `redeem`, or any
escrow function, which stay permissionless.
